relations.quote: These rows are the suffixes of [Address fields and array layout on tapes](address-fields.md), so the network acts on rows indexed by those fields.

symbols.name: number of roles
symbols.meaning: The number of roles, the wires' fixed places in the network, over which rows are distributed.
symbols.quote: Let $W$ be the number of roles.

symbols.name: role permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation of roles that the scalar network applies, sending input role w to output role rho(w).
symbols.quote: Let $\rho$ be the permutation of roles that it applies: an input at role $w$ leaves at output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w \in \{+1,-1\}$.

symbols.name: input role
symbols.meaning: An input role of the scalar network, whose value is moved to output role rho(w).
symbols.quote: Let $\rho$ be the permutation of roles that it applies: an input at role $w$ leaves at output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w \in \{+1,-1\}$.

symbols.name: route sign
symbols.meaning: The sign, +1 or -1, carried by the route from input role w to output role rho(w).
symbols.quote: Let $\rho$ be the permutation of roles that it applies: an input at role $w$ leaves at output role $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w \in \{+1,-1\}$.

symbols.name: network node
symbols.meaning: A source, gate or sink of the network, which carries one frame.
symbols.quote: Each source, gate and sink $\nu$ carries an invertible linear operator $D_\nu$ on arrays indexed by the common address set, its *frame*.

symbols.name: frame
symbols.meaning: The invertible linear operator carried by node nu, acting on arrays indexed by the common address set.
symbols.quote: Each source, gate and sink $\nu$ carries an invertible linear operator $D_\nu$ on arrays indexed by the common address set, its *frame*.

symbols.name: edge tail
symbols.meaning: The node at which an edge starts.
symbols.quote: Along an edge from node $\alpha$ to node $\beta$ the stored array changes by $D_\beta D_\alpha^{-1}$.

symbols.name: edge head
symbols.meaning: The node at which an edge ends.
symbols.quote: Along an edge from node $\alpha$ to node $\beta$ the stored array changes by $D_\beta D_\alpha^{-1}$.

symbols.name: logical array
symbols.meaning: The logical array that a node stores in the form D_nu f.
symbols.quote: The stored array at $\nu$ is $D_\nu f$ when the logical array is $f$.

symbols.name: pointwise gate
symbols.meaning: A pointwise linear gate, which combines its input arrays at each address with fixed scalar coefficients.
symbols.quote: A pointwise linear gate $G$ combines its $p$ input arrays $f_1,\dots,f_p$ at each address with fixed scalar coefficients.

symbols.name: gate input count
symbols.meaning: The number of input arrays of a gate, counting the arrays it combines.
symbols.quote: A pointwise linear gate $G$ combines its $p$ input arrays $f_1,\dots,f_p$ at each address with fixed scalar coefficients.

symbols.name: row index
symbols.meaning: The index of a row at a fixed prefix, which selects the role that receives the row.
symbols.quote: Distribute the rows cyclically: row $\ell$, the $\ell$th row at a fixed prefix, goes to role $\ell \bmod W$, after the row count for each prefix is padded to a multiple of $W$.

symbols.name: identity operator
symbols.meaning: The identity operator, which leaves every array unchanged.
symbols.quote: Here $I$ is the identity operator, which leaves every array unchanged.
